- We used our team-template for the MSA but left some Redwood-specific fields blank (signer info / billing).
- We expect this to be a 3-month pilot, ~50k tokens/month, US hosting only — but confirm if Redwood needs specific regional language.

Can you confirm whether Redwood prefers to (A) adopt our MSA and you submit redlines, or (B) switch to Redwood's template and we scope changes? We'd also like to schedule a 30-minute kickoff to walk parties and expected timeline.

Thanks Ellis — received both attachments and appreciate the context.

High-level response / proposed approach:

1) We prefer to start with your draft and produce a redline back to you (option A).
2) We'll run a quick template alignment (mapping your clauses to our standard MSA) to identify gaps that affect delivery or billing.
3) Internal owners: Kimberly — privacy/security and evidence items; Jonas — template fit, signing authority, and billing exhibits.

Could you confirm the following so we can prioritize:
- Is the expected hosting region strictly US-only? Any EU/APAC residency needs?
- Will NorthForge require SOC2 audit evidence or a security questionnaire response as part of procurement?
- Who should we expect as the billing contact and PO approver (name + email)?

Proposed timeline: initial redline summary (high-level flags) by EOD tomorrow; full redline within 5 business days pending any escalations. If that works, I'll circulate the summary and a short action plan.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NorthForge MSA - initial flags

Folks — quick internal triage after a first pass on northforge_MSA_draft_v1.docx. I took the parts most likely to drive negotiation.

Priority flags (short):
- Data residency / audit: MSA lacks explicit residency warranty; if they expect US-only, we can accept but need to confirm. If they ask for EU or multi-region, that raises infra and compliance changes.
- Indemnity & liability caps: Their indemnity is fairly broad; recommend we limit to direct damages and keep liability cap at the order form value (pilot amount) unless sales agrees to higher cap.
- Audit & access: Their audit language includes broad rights. Ask for scoping (90-day notice, but limit to tech/security third-party audits).
- PCI / regulated scope: They mention PCI in order form notes — clarify if pilot touches cardholder data. If yes, escalate to legal.
- Exhibit A: pricing present but missing SOW language about token measurement and billing cadence — Jonas to map token metric to pricing line items.

Suggested immediate actions:
- Chloe: confirm hosting region and billing contact with Ellis (you set).
- Jonas: produce an Exhibit A checklist mapping to our billing model.
- I will prepare a pared-down redline summary (attachment) with risk-tiered notes for Legal.

Attaching redline_summary_template.pdf for internal use; will convert to customer-facing summary once we agree on approach.

kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts & Risk, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

- Jonas attached an Exhibit A checklist (token metrics, billing cadence) for your review.

Action items / mutual plan:
1) NorthForge: confirm hosting region (US-only?) and provide billing contact (name + email) — requested by Wed 5/20.
2) Redwood: send customer-facing redline (PDF) with our proposed edits by Fri 5/21.
3) Both: 30-min alignment call to review redlines and signer path — suggest Thu 5/20 at 10:00am PT (please confirm).

Links & attachments:
- redline_summary_template.pdf (attached)
- exhibitA_party_sheet.xlsx (attached)

If you confirm the 10:00am PT slot I'll send a calendar invite. Looking forward to moving this quickly.
